flags: The literal rule (flag if MTD terminations fall BELOW baseline+500) does not trip — 31,551 is well above the 18,422.5 threshold. But that rule was designed to catch drops, not spikes, and 31,551 is 76% above the 2-month baseline average — reporting this as a quiet green/amber would misrepresent a genuinely large anomaly, so this is being flagged red on judgement rather than the letter of the rule.

Full calendar-month uConnect termination totals have climbed for four consecutive months: Apr 20,745 → May 44,676 → Jun 72,487 → Jul 84,803 → Aug (month-to-date) 35,179. This is roughly a 4x increase from April to July and does not look like the isolated one-off May batch-load event previously suspected (see memory) — it reads as an ongoing, worsening pattern. Needs business/data-team investigation into what's driving the growth, not just a data-shape footnote.

Within August itself, only 11,491 of the 31,551 day-1-20 terminations (36%) had landed by day 14, with the remaining 20,060 (64%) landing in just days 15-20 — consistent with lumpy, batch-style backdated loading rather than smooth day-by-day churn. Treat the exact day-cutoff figure with caution, but the underlying multi-month volume growth is not explained by cutoff timing alone.
